rules.sentence: Typical symptoms include diarrhea (often associated with blood and/or mucus), abdominal pain, and signs of bowel obstructions.
Perirectal fistulas may be present on the exam which may help to clue the physician into the diagnosis.
Patients often present with abdominal pain, diarrhea, and hematochezia.
Other signs that may aid diagnosis are weight loss and pallor secondary to anemia.
